summary:
EARTHWATCH AI is an interactive global environmental monitoring and multi-hazard screening dashboard powered by a FastAPI backend and a self-contained HTML, CSS, and JavaScript frontend. It enables users to explore global risk profiles through an interactive map featuring 177 country boundaries, 243 city markers, and multi-level administrative drill-downs down to states and districts.

Environmental and disaster data is often scattered across separate agencies, making rapid situational awareness difficult. EARTHWATCH AI addresses this challenge by aggregating real-time feeds from USGS, NASA EONET, GDACS, NOAA SWPC, NASA/JPL, and Open-Meteo into a single unified interface. Users can inspect seven-day weather trends, filter across 23 distinct hazard categories, customize AI screening thresholds, share location-specific URLs, and export findings in JSON or CSV formats.

This unified tool is important because it makes complex geospatial and hazard intelligence accessible without heavy GIS software. By combining multi-scale mapping, automated caching, and live environmental feeds into a lightweight web application, EARTHWATCH AI helps researchers, planners, and communities quickly screen regional vulnerabilities and monitor emerging natural events.
details:
EARTHWATCH AI is a compact global weather-risk screening and multi-hazard monitoring dashboard built with a Python FastAPI backend and an interactive HTML, CSS, and JavaScript frontend.

Key Features & Architecture:

- Global & Local Interactive Mapping: Displays 177 country and territory polygons alongside 243 populated city markers sourced from Natural Earth. Users can click countries, select cities, or drill down through administrative boundaries (ADM1 states/regions and ADM2 districts/municipalities) powered by geoBoundaries.

- 23-Category Multi-Hazard Screening: Evaluates 23 distinct natural hazard categories within a configurable radius (50 km to 1,000 km). The system strictly separates observed live reports from weather-derived screening proxies and explicitly marks categories without verified local feeds (such as sinkholes or epidemics) as unavailable.

- Transparent Weather-Risk Proxies: Samples seven-day daily precipitation, maximum/minimum temperature, and wind speed observations from Open-Meteo to compute weighted screening scores (0.00 to 1.00) for Flood, Fire, Drought, and Overall Risk.

- Operational Intelligence & Exports: Features country search by name or ISO code, risk-level sorting, seven-day weather trend charts (°C/°F), configurable alert thresholds, browser notifications, shareable coordinate links, and one-click CSV/JSON data exports.

- Performance & Caching: Uses multi-threaded API fetching and tiered caching (30 minutes for global overviews, 15 minutes for hazard feeds, and 24 hours for city and boundary geometries) for fast, responsive exploration.
